description: A worked calibration set: twelve candidate outputs and the grades a careful author gave them, spanning the scale. Grading twelve samples is a real sitting, and this set exists so a fresh install can show the whole calibration path without one.

## What write-ahead logging is

SQLite normally writes changes by copying the original pages into a rollback journal and then editing the database file. With write-ahead logging it does the opposite: new pages go into a separate `-wal` file, and the database file is left alone until a checkpoint folds them in.

```sql
PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;
```

## Why readers and a writer coexist

A reader takes the database file plus the WAL frames committed before it started. A writer appends new frames. Neither blocks the other, because they are not writing to the same bytes.

## What it costs

A checkpoint has to run eventually, and until it does the WAL grows. Readers on a network filesystem cannot share the WAL index, so WAL is a local-disk mode.

## Write-ahead logging

In WAL mode SQLite appends changes to a `-wal` file instead of rewriting the database in place.

```sql
PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;
```

## Concurrency

Readers see a snapshot; one writer appends. They do not block each other.

## Cost

The WAL grows until a checkpoint, and it does not work over a network filesystem.

## WAL

WAL means the database writes ahead. This makes it faster because writing ahead is faster than writing behind.

```sql
PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;
```

## Concurrency

Multiple writers can write at the same time, which is the main benefit.

## Write-ahead logging in SQLite

Changes are appended to a separate log file and folded back into the database at a checkpoint.

```sql
PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;
PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint=1000;
```

## Why it helps

Readers read a consistent snapshot of the database plus the frames committed before they began. A single writer appends. Because the two touch different bytes, a long read no longer blocks a write.

## What it costs

The WAL file grows between checkpoints, and the shared-memory index it needs rules out network filesystems.

## Overview

SQLite's write-ahead log is a file called `-wal`. Instead of a rollback journal, committed pages are appended there.

```sql
PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;
```

## Trade-offs

You get concurrent reads with a writer. You pay for it with a second file, a checkpoint, and no network filesystem support. Also, WAL mode is persistent across connections, which surprises people.

## What is a database?

A database is a place to store information. SQLite is a database. Write-ahead logging is a feature of SQLite.

```sql
PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;
```

## More

It makes things faster.

## Write-ahead logging

Committed pages are appended to a `-wal` sidecar and checkpointed into the main file later.

```sql
PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;
```

## Concurrency

One writer, many readers, no blocking between them. Readers use a shared-memory index (`-shm`) to find frames.

## Costs

Checkpoint pauses, WAL growth under long-running readers, and no network filesystems.

## WAL mode

WAL keeps a log of changes. Readers and writers can both work. Set it like this:

```sql
PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;
```

The main downside is that the log file can get big.

## Write-ahead logging

SQLite writes changed pages to a separate file first. A checkpoint moves them back.

```sql
PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;
```

## Concurrency

Readers are not blocked by the writer. The writer is not blocked by readers, although a checkpoint can be.

## Costs

WAL growth, checkpoint work, local disk only.

## Journaling

SQLite supports several journal modes, including DELETE, TRUNCATE, PERSIST, MEMORY, WAL and OFF. WAL stands for write-ahead logging and was added in version 3.7.0.

```sql
PRAGMA journal_mode;
```

Each mode has different durability characteristics which are documented in the SQLite manual.

## Write-ahead logging

With WAL, SQLite appends to a log and periodically checkpoints. This allows readers and a writer to proceed concurrently because readers never see partially written pages.

```sql
PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;
```

## Cost

The log grows and must be checkpointed. WAL also requires all processes to be on the same host.

## WAL

Write-ahead logging removes the need for locking entirely, so any number of writers can commit at once without coordination.

```sql
PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;
```

There is no downside.

reference_jury.description: A deterministic jury that reproduces the author's own grade with an alternating one-point scatter. It is not a model; it exists so a shipped calibration set has a figure that can be reproduced exactly on any machine, with no GPU and no network.
